objective: Evaluate whether an audited, bounded Graph can replace or reorder R0 Claim slots under the same visible budget and create an explainable quality/cost Pareto improvement without hard regressions.

implementation.claimCountPolicy: R1 primary and co-evidence ceilings equal R0; Graph replaces or reorders and cannot append capacity.

offlineResult.limitations: Relevance review did not claim answer benefit and used revealed Dev questions.

replacementCases.finding: Relevant replacement, no answer gain, higher cost.
Relevant replacement, no answer gain, higher cost.
Relevant replacement removed unrelated convergence modes, but the answer was already saturated and cost increased.

additionalHardFailure.finding: R1 emitted two evidence identifiers absent from its context while R0 used resolvable Claim identifiers. This is an observed target hard regression.

devCore.reason: The pre-registered contract forbids Dev Core when the answer Micro gate fails. Running it would spend quota and weaken the experimental contract rather than add admissible evidence.

decision.production: Keep R0 as the online default. Do not enable this R1 policy.
decision.graphInfrastructure: Retain audited Graph for governance, impact analysis and bounded candidate diagnostics; the failed online selector does not invalidate the Graph substrate.
decision.nextHypothesis: A future R1 must prove marginal task utility before replacement, account for closed Claim+Evidence size during ranking, and avoid reordering unchanged sets unless expected utility exceeds cost. It requires a new frozen contract and run; current Dev questions remain regression assets.

limitations: Questions are revealed single-domain Dev assets and the judge is an AI proxy.
One post-hoc adjudication corrected a judge application error that was contradicted by the frozen scoring contract; raw output remains immutable.
The correction made R1 worse relative to R0 and therefore cannot create a deceptive positive reward.
No Dev Core or blind generalization claim is made.
